note: Guide lines from a helper pattern to al-Jady are modern UFUQ teaching constructions (decision D-4, MODERN_PEDAGOGICAL); no local source attests them as historical methods. Only al-Jady's use for direction finding is historically attested, and it is cited separately as historical context, never as a modern Qibla or navigation algorithm.

labels.gloss: the direction of the geodetic north meridian at the observer (azimuth 0)

citations.locator: ADR-003 fixed conventions: azimuth clockwise from True North

relationships.explanation: UFUQ guide line (a modern teaching aid): from the middle star of the hand, follow the line down towards the northern horizon to reach al-Jady.

citations.supports: the helper-to-al-Jady line is accepted only as MODERN_PEDAGOGICAL content

relationships.explanation: UFUQ guide line (a modern teaching aid, the familiar 'pointer stars' method): continue the line through the two end stars of the box to reach al-Jady.

citations.supports: greater Banat Nash as the alternative route; the guide line is MODERN_PEDAGOGICAL

relationships.explanation: al-Jady lies close to the north celestial pole, so the point on the horizon directly below it is close to True North. al-Jady is a star cue; True North is a direction on the ground, and they are not the same thing.

historicalContext.text: Arabic anwa literature records al-Jady being used to find direction.

citations.supports: al-Jady used for direction finding and Qibla inference (historical context only)
